BiblicalUsage: The word saʻar means a tempest; also a terror. It stands in Ezekiel 27:35, "…sore afraid, they shall be troubled in countenance", and in Isaiah 28:2, "…destroying storm, as a flood of mighty waters…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God put saʻar here on purpose, and I take his word for it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
